thread:
SRE-Bot: ALERT: Elevated 5xx rate observed in eu-west1 gateway (rolling 5m = 7.2%, baseline 0.3%). Auto-paging to #incidents. Links: https://dash.redwood/eu-west1/errors, runbook: https://confluence/redwood/runbooks/gateway-5xx

Jamie: acked. Jumping in. pinging oncall and infra.

Alex P: I’m on call for infra. grabbing the logs, will check upstream LB and envoy stats.

Maria (oncall): I’m the primary oncall. Confirmed customer-facing errors — several low-latency requests returning 502/504. Impact: ~4% of requests for some tenants, elevated error spike started ~3m ago. Notifying support.

Ryan: seeing a correlated spike in egress timeouts to model-backend pool eu-west1-ml-01. 95th latency to ml workers jumps from 60ms -> 2.1s. Possible slow downstream.

Jamie: good find. Can you paste the `curl` check you ran?

Ryan: sure — health probe against ml worker:
```
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}s" https://ml-eu1.internal/health
# returned: 200 2.08s
```

Alex P: envoy upstream host health shows high pending requests and retries for pool eu-west1-ml-*. Might be a small subset of workers flapping and causing circuit-breaker tripping.

Ops-Bot: AUTOMATED: Circuit breaker tripped on route /v1/generate -> backend ml-eu1 cluster at 4187654330 (automatic cooldown started).

Jamie: ok, we need to reduce client pressure on the bad pool and failover to eu-west1-ml-02/03 or cross-region fallback to us-east1 if necessary. First step: disable new routing to affected pool and enable overflow to healthy pool. Maria, coordinate with prod.

Maria (oncall): doing a quick mitigation: enabling routing policy `overflow:enabled` for gateway eu-west1, TTL 10m. Command: `rdctl routing set --region eu-west1 --policy overflow=on --ttl 600`

Alex P: i’m going to drain the suspected hosts in cluster ml-eu1 (hosts 10.12.8.4 and 10.12.8.5) and trigger a recycling of the worker processes. Running: `kubectl cordon` + `kubectl rollout restart deployment/ml-worker` for those nodes.

Ryan: note — there’s also an increase in Redis latency for eu-west1 cache shards. Could be amplification: slow ml backends causing more cache contention. See mem stats: `redis-cluster latency p95=150ms (norm 3ms)`.

Jamie: escalate if we see cache saturation. For now, mitigation plan order: 1) enable overflow routing 2) drain/flap suspected ml workers 3) if errors persist > 15m, steer traffic to us-east1 fallback pool (gradual). Also inform support/customer-impact.

Tina: support here — notifying the top 5 enterprise customers in eu-west region with the following message: "We are investigating elevated errors in eu-west; there may be intermittent 5xx responses. We will update within 30 minutes." Any ETA?

Maria (oncall): ETA 15-30m depending on worker recycle. I'll update status page.

Ops-Bot: NOTE: Network autoscaler added capacity to eu-west1 gateway at 4187654380 (scale event).

Alex P: drain commands issued at 4187654485. Restarting 2 pods now.

Ryan: after restart, ml worker p95 latency back to ~80ms for two nodes; overall cluster p95 down to 120ms. Error rate dropped to 1.4% within next 4m.

Jamie: good progress. Monitoring for 10 more minutes. We should still prepare a controlled cross-region shift if bursts repeat. Can someone validate session affinity and statefulness for fallback?

Alex P: session affinity handled by token hashing; fallback to us-east will use model-variant `v1-fallback` which is stateless for generation. Safe to shift small percentage.

Maria (oncall): initiating gradual traffic steer: `rdctl traffic steer --from eu-west1 --to us-east1 --percent 5 --duration 5m`

SRE-Bot: AUTOMATED: Traffic steering executed at 4187654950 -> 5% to us-east1.

Tina: forwarding an internal note to GA customers: "Traffic has been partially rerouted to us-east to reduce errors. No data loss expected. Expect slightly higher latencies for affected requests."

Jamie: monitoring metrics: error-rate now down to 0.6% overall, eu-west1 residual 0.9%. p95 latency bumped for those 5% to us-east at ~180ms (expected). Good tradeoff.

Ryan: digging into root cause — suspect recent release of ml-worker 2.14 introduced a memory leak under certain request patterns. I see OOM kills on a minority of pods before restart. Rolling back to 2.13 on the problematic nodes might prevent recurrence.

Alex P: can we pin the deployment to 2.13 for eu-west1 only while we fix 2.14? `kubectl set image deployment/ml-worker ml-worker=ml-worker:2.13 --namespace=prod --record`

Maria (oncall): doing the pin now, rolling update started at 4187655120.

Ops-Bot: AUTOMATED: Rollback/rollout events: deployment ml-worker -> image ml-worker:2.13 at 4187655135.

Jamie: excellent. Let's keep the overflow routing on until we've validated stability for 30 minutes. Also create a follow-up ticket and postmortem assignment.

Tina: support update sent to customers. One customer reported a failed job; opened a case and linked to incident.

Ryan: after the rollback and restarts, cluster p95 back to baseline; error rate stable at 0.2% for last 8m. Looks resolved from infrastructure side.

Jamie: moving to monitoring -> we'll keep incident channel open for follow-up actions. Begin incident timeline notes for postmortem. Key actions: overflow routing enabled (4187654335), drain/restart pods (4187654485), traffic steer 5% (4187654950), rollback to 2.13 (4187655120).

Maria (oncall): handing off to Jamie at 4187656121 for follow-up and postmortem drafting. I’m dropping off.

Jamie: taking over. Thanks all. Next: owner for postmortem and blameless RCA? Ryan can own the RCA (root cause: memory leak in 2.14), Alex P to own mitigation (canary/qs), Tina to own customer comms. I'll set the follow-up ticket and link runbook and relevant logs.

Ops-Bot: INCIDENT: Severity downgraded to SEV3 at 4187656121.

Jamie: closing thread for live mitigation, keeping open for postmortem comments. :thumbsup:
